ثُمَّ إِنِّى دَعَوْتُهُمْ جِهَارًا
ثُمَّ إِنِّىٓ أَعْلَنتُ لَهُمْ وَأَسْرَرْتُ لَهُمْ إِسْرَارًا

يُرْسِلِ ٱلسَّمَآءَ عَلَيْكُم مِّدْرَارًا

مَّا لَكُمْ لَا تَرْجُونَ لِلَّهِ وَقَارًا
وَقَدْ خَلَقَكُمْ أَطْوَارًا
أَلَمْ تَرَوْا۟ كَيْفَ خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ سَبْعَ سَمَٰوَٰتٍ طِبَاقًا

وَٱللَّهُ أَنۢبَتَكُم مِّنَ ٱلْأَرْضِ نَبَاتًا
ثُمَّ يُعِيدُكُمْ فِيهَا وَيُخْرِجُكُمْ إِخْرَاجًا
وَٱللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلْأَرْضَ بِسَاطًا
لِّتَسْلُكُوا۟ مِنْهَا سُبُلًا فِجَاجًا

وَمَكَرُوا۟ مَكْرًا كُبَّارًا

leads.title: Flood narratives across traditions
leads.summary: A divinely sent flood with a chosen survivor appears in Sumerian, Akkadian, Hebrew, Quranic, Vedic, Greek, and Chinese sources. The Near Eastern versions are historically linked; the others are candidate convergences.

evidence.text: Specificity test: the bird-release sequence (Gilgamesh XI; Genesis 8) is a rare motif combination that marks the Mesopotamian–Hebrew link. The Quran has no bird release.
Noah's drowned son (Quran 11:42–43) has no Genesis counterpart and is a sub-lead.
The Chinese story is about controlling the flood, not surviving it, so it is a weak match.

leads.title: Utnapishtim's flood (Gilgamesh, Standard Babylonian Tablet XI:8-206) ↔ Noah's preaching, the five idols and the flood

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: All others perish (weight 5.9); Hero privately warned of the coming flood by a deity (weight 5.8). Pair score 11.7.

Only in Utnapishtim's flood (Gilgamesh, Standard Babylonian Tablet XI:8-206): The divine warning commands: abandon riches, spurn property and save life; After the flood all humankind has returned to clay; the plain is flat as a roof; Instead of the flood, a lion, a wolf, famine or plague should have diminished the people; The mother goddess bars the god who caused the flood from the offering, for he acted without counsel; Huge measured quantities of bitumen, pitch and oil are poured into the kiln and the hull; The hero slaughters oxen and sheep and gives the workers beer, oil and wine like river water, so they feast as at the New Year festival; What sets the flood in motion: God's decision on violence, or the rejected prophet's prayer; The chief god sees the boat and is enraged that a living being escaped: 'no man should survive!'; What the ark contains; Besides kin and animals, craftsmen of every skill are taken aboard; The god gives the hero a cover story: Enlil hates me, I am going down to the Apsû, and he will rain abundance on you (bread-cakes in the morning, a torrent of wheat in the evening) - an ambiguous promise of the coming flood; How the ark is described; and 79 more.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֜ים לְנֹ֗חַ קֵ֤ץ כָּל בָּשָׂר֙ בָּ֣א לְפָנַ֔י כִּֽי מָלְאָ֥ה הָאָ֛רֶץ חָמָ֖ס מִפְּנֵיהֶ֑ם וְהִנְנִ֥י מַשְׁחִיתָ֖ם אֶת הָאָֽרֶץ
וַיַּ֖עַשׂ נֹ֑חַ כְּ֠כֹל אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֥ה אֹת֛וֹ אֱלֹהִ֖ים כֵּ֥ן עָשָֽׂה
قَالَ يَٰقَوْمِ إِنِّى لَكُمْ نَذِيرٌ مُّبِينٌ
أَنِ ٱعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَٱتَّقُوهُ وَأَطِيعُونِ
قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّى دَعَوْتُ قَوْمِى لَيْلًا وَنَهَارًا

matches.label: Destruction motivated by human wickedness or violence
matches.note: Motive changed: Genesis gives moral corruption and violence (rabbāh rāʿat hā-ʾādām ... wa-ttimmālēʾ hā-ʾāreṣ ḥāmās; hišḥît kol bāśār ʾet darkô). Q 71 gives rejection of the messenger and idolatry: rabbi innahum ʿaṣawnī ... wa-qālū lā tadharunna ālihatakum wa-lā tadharunna waddan wa-lā suwāʿan wa-lā yaghūtha wa-yaʿūqa wa-nasrā. Five named gods; Genesis names no god but YHWH/Elohim.

passages.text: וַיַּ֣רְא יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֥י רַבָּ֛ה רָעַ֥ת הָאָדָ֖ם בָּאָ֑רֶץ וְכָל יֵ֨צֶר֙ מַחְשְׁבֹ֣ת לִבּ֔וֹ רַ֥ק רַ֖ע כָּל הַיּֽוֹם
וַתִּשָּׁחֵ֥ת הָאָ֖רֶץ לִפְנֵ֣י הָֽאֱלֹהִ֑ים וַתִּמָּלֵ֥א הָאָ֖רֶץ חָמָֽס
וַיַּ֧רְא אֱלֹהִ֛ים אֶת הָאָ֖רֶץ וְהִנֵּ֣ה נִשְׁחָ֑תָה כִּֽי הִשְׁחִ֧ית כָּל בָּשָׂ֛ר אֶת דַּרְכּ֖וֹ עַל הָאָֽרֶץ
قَالَ نُوحٌ رَّبِّ إِنَّهُمْ عَصَوْنِى وَٱتَّبَعُوا۟ مَن لَّمْ يَزِدْهُ مَالُهُۥ وَوَلَدُهُۥٓ إِلَّا خَسَارًا
وَقَالُوا۟ لَا تَذَرُنَّ ءَالِهَتَكُمْ وَلَا تَذَرُنَّ وَدًّا وَلَا سُوَاعًا وَلَا يَغُوثَ وَيَعُوقَ وَنَسْرًا
وَقَدْ أَضَلُّوا۟ كَثِيرًا وَلَا تَزِدِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ إِلَّا ضَلَٰلًا

matches.label: Hero asks the deity to judge or destroy his opponents
matches.note: Who calls for destruction is reversed: in Genesis God decides alone (wa-yyōʾmer YHWH ʾemḥeh ʾet hā-ʾādām; we-hinnî mašḥîtām ʾet hā-ʾāreṣ) and even regrets creating (wa-yyinnāḥem YHWH). In Q 71:26-27 Noah asks: rabbi lā tadhar ʿalā l-arḍi mina l-kāfirīna dayyāran, innaka in tadharhum yuḍillū ʿibādaka. There is no divine regret in the Quran.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֗ה אֶמְחֶ֨ה אֶת הָאָדָ֤ם אֲשֶׁר בָּרָ֨אתִי֙ מֵעַל֙ פְּנֵ֣י הָֽאֲדָמָ֔ה מֵֽאָדָם֙ עַד בְּהֵמָ֔ה עַד רֶ֖מֶשׂ וְעַד ע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם כִּ֥י נִחַ֖מְתִּי כִּ֥י עֲשִׂיתִֽם
וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֜ים לְנֹ֗חַ קֵ֤ץ כָּל בָּשָׂר֙ בָּ֣א לְפָנַ֔י כִּֽי מָלְאָ֥ה הָאָ֛רֶץ חָמָ֖ס מִפְּנֵיהֶ֑ם וְהִנְנִ֥י מַשְׁחִיתָ֖ם אֶת הָאָֽרֶץ
وَقَالَ نُوحٌ رَّبِّ لَا تَذَرْ عَلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ دَيَّارًا
إِنَّكَ إِن تَذَرْهُمْ يُضِلُّوا۟ عِبَادَكَ وَلَا يَلِدُوٓا۟ إِلَّا فَاجِرًا كَفَّارًا

matches.label: Seek forgiveness and repent, and God will send the sky down on you in abundant rain
matches.note: Rain reversed: in Genesis rain from opened sky is the destruction (wa-ʾărubbōt ha-ššāmayim niftāḥû, wa-yehî ha-ggešem ʿal hā-ʾāreṣ ʾarbāʿîm yôm). Noah in Q 71:10-11 promises rain as blessing if they repent: istaghfirū rabbakum ... yursili s-samāʾa ʿalaykum midrāran, then (71:25) mimmā khaṭīʾātihim ughriqū: the sky that could have blessed them drowns them.

passages.text: בִּשְׁנַ֨ת שֵׁשׁ מֵא֤וֹת שָׁנָה֙ לְחַיֵּי נֹ֔חַ בַּחֹ֨דֶשׁ֙ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י בְּשִׁבְעָֽה עָשָׂ֥ר י֖וֹם לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֗ה נִבְקְעוּ֙ כָּֽל מַעְיְנֹת֙ תְּה֣וֹם רַבָּ֔ה וַאֲרֻבֹּ֥ת הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם נִפְתָּֽחוּ
וַֽיְהִ֥י הַגֶּ֖שֶׁם עַל הָאָ֑רֶץ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים י֔וֹם וְאַרְבָּעִ֖ים לָֽיְלָה
فَقُلْتُ ٱسْتَغْفِرُوا۟ رَبَّكُمْ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ غَفَّارًا

matches.label: Hero's family saved with him
matches.note: The saved are defined by faith, not by house: Gen 7:1 bōʾ ʾattāh we-kol bêtkā ʾel ha-ttēvāh kî ʾōtkā rāʾîtî ṣaddîq. Q 71:28 rabbi ghfir lī wa-li-wālidayya wa-li-man dakhala baytiya muʾminan wa-li-l-muʾminīna wa-l-muʾmināt: whoever enters my house as a believer.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ לְנֹ֔חַ בֹּֽא אַתָּ֥ה וְכָל בֵּיתְךָ֖ אֶל הַתֵּבָ֑ה כִּֽי אֹתְךָ֥ רָאִ֛יתִי צַדִּ֥יק לְפָנַ֖י בַּדּ֥וֹר הַזֶּֽה
וַיָּ֣בֹא נֹ֗חַ וּ֠בָנָיו וְאִשְׁתּ֧וֹ וּנְשֵֽׁי בָנָ֛יו אִתּ֖וֹ אֶל הַתֵּבָ֑ה מִפְּנֵ֖י מֵ֥י הַמַּבּֽוּל
رَّبِّ ٱغْفِرْ لِى وَلِوَٰلِدَىَّ وَلِمَن دَخَلَ بَيْتِىَ مُؤْمِنًا وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَٱلْمُؤْمِنَٰتِ وَلَا تَزِدِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ إِلَّا تَبَارًۢا

matches.label: Deity resolves or promises not to repeat the destruction
matches.note: Ending changed: Genesis ends with Noah's sacrifice and God's promise lōʾ ʾōsîf leqallēl ʿôd ʾet hā-ʾădāmāh ... we-lōʾ ʾōsîf ʿôd lehakkôt ʾet kol ḥay. Q 71 ends with the drowned sent on into fire (ughriqū fa-udkhilū nāran) and Noah's prayer of forgiveness and of destruction (wa-lā tazidi ẓ-ẓālimīna illā tabārā). No sacrifice, no covenant, no 'never again'.

مِّمَّا خَطِيٓـَٰٔتِهِمْ أُغْرِقُوا۟ فَأُدْخِلُوا۟ نَارًا فَلَمْ يَجِدُوا۟ لَهُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَنصَارًا

Only in Ziusudra (Eridu Genesis, ETCSL 1.7.4, segments C-E): The flood storm rages for seven days and seven nights; A goddess laments the destruction of the people decreed by the gods; The sun god appears after the flood and shines into the boat through an opening the hero makes; Animals taken aboard (no pairing specified); The gods grant the flood hero life like a god, eternal life; The flood hero is settled in a far land (Dilmun) where the sun rises; The gods are made to swear an oath binding them to the decision to destroy humankind; Warning spoken to a wall or reed hut so the hero overhears; The verdict of the divine assembly to destroy is declared irrevocable; Seventh ancestor walks with God and is taken without dying; Hero blessed on leaving the vessel; Hero singled out as righteous or pious; and 5 more.

Only in Noah's preaching, the five idols and the flood: Because of their sins they were drowned and then made to enter a fire; The people put their fingers in their ears and wrap their garments over their heads to avoid hearing the prophet; Noah's people refuse to abandon their gods Wadd, Suwa', Yaghuth, Ya'uq and Nasr; The flood hero prays for forgiveness for himself, his parents, whoever enters his house believing, and all believers; God caused humans to grow from the earth like a plant, returns them to it and will bring them out again; Prophet summons his people night and day, openly and in secret, yet they only flee further; People are put into the earth and brought out of it again [divergence between the texts]; Destroying a people together with their offspring because of their character [neutral] [divergence between the texts]; Human comes from dust and returns to dust [divergence between the texts]; Before the flood the hero tells his city that heaven will rain plenty on them [divergence between the texts]; A wish that no one be left alive by the destruction [divergence between the texts]; Deity resolves or promises not to repeat the destruction [divergence between the texts]; and 18 more.
